    #Tutorial 1 (Heat Engines & Refrigerators)

    #Question 1

    W˙out​=Q˙​H​−Q˙​L​−Q˙​waste​

    W˙out​=280−145−8

    W˙out​=127 GJ/h=35.3 MW

    ηth​=Q˙​H​W˙​=280127​

    ηth​=0.45357=45.4%

    #Question 2

    COPR​=W˙in​Q˙​L​​

    1.5=W˙in​60​

    W˙in​=40 kJ/min=0.67 kW

    Q˙​H​=Q˙​L​+W˙in​

    Q˙​H​=60+40

    Q˙​H​=100 kJ/min

    #Question 3

    To maintain constant T in the house, Qgain​=Qloss​.

    Q˙​H​=60000−4000=56000 kJ/h

    COPHP​=W˙in​Q˙​H​​

    2.5=W˙in​56000​

    W˙in​=22400 kJ/h=6.22 kW

    Efficiency when environmental temperature increases

    #Tutorial 2 (Carnot Cycle & Entropy)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    COPR​=Win​QL​​=QH​−QL​QL​​=QL​QH​​−11​=TL​TH​​−11​=1.2−11​=5

    Since a Carnot refrigeration cycle is reversible, QL​QH​​ can be replaced with TL​TH​​.

    QL​=COPR​⋅Win​

    QL​=5(22)=110 kJ (heat absorbed from refrigerated space)

    QH​=QL​+Win​

    QH​=110+22=132 kJ (heat rejected to environment)

    Using the first law of thermodynamics for the condenser,

    Q−W=mΔh

    QH​=m(h4​−h3​)

    h4​−h3​=mQ​

    Since state 3 is saturated vapor and state 4 is saturated liquid, h4​−h3​=hfg​.

    Enthalpy of vaporization is then,

    hfg​=0.96132​=137.5 kJ/kg

    From Table A11,

    At T=60°C, hfg​=139.09 kJ/kg

    At T=65°C, hfg​=132.05 kJ/kg

    65−60TH​−60​=132.05−130.09137.5−139.09​

    TH​=61.129°C=334.13 K

    TH​=1.2TL​

    TL​=1.2334.13​=278.44 K=5.4411°C

    From Table A11,

    At T=4°C, Psat​=337.9 kPa

    At T=6°C, Psat​=362.23 kPa

    362.23−337.9PL​−337.9​=6−45.4411−4​

    PL​=355.43 kPa=0.355 MPa

    #Part (b)

    State 1: T1​=TL​ and P1​=PL​ (enters evaporator as liquid-vapor mixture)

    State 2: T2​=T1​ and P2​=P1​ (enters compressor as liquid-vapor mixture)

    State 3: T3​=TH​ and P3​=PH​ (enters condenser as saturated vapor)

    State 4: T4​=T3​ and P4​=P3​ (enters turbine as saturated liquid)

    #Question 2

    Assumptions:

    • Air can be treated as an ideal gas
    • Steady-state, steady flow system
    • Isothermal, internally reversible process

    Using first law of thermodynamics,

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙Δh

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙cp​ΔT

    Since air temperature is constant,

    Q˙​=W˙=−30 kW (negative sign indicates work input)

    ΔS˙sys​=T0​Q˙​​=25+273−30​=−0.10067 kW/K

    ΔS˙surr​=TQ˙​​=17+27330​=0.10345 kW/K

    S˙gen​=0.10345−0.10067=0.0027771 kW/K

    Since S˙gen​>0, it complies with the increase in entropy principle.

    #Question 3

    COPHP​=W˙in​Q˙​H​​=Q˙​H​−Q˙​L​Q˙​H​​=1−Q˙​H​Q˙​L​​1​=1−TH​TL​​1​

    COPHP​=1−24+2737+273​1​=17.471

    W˙in​=17.471300​=17.172 kW (work input to heat pump)

    Q˙​H​=300 kW (heat gain by high-temperature source)

    Q˙​L​=300−17.172=282.83 kW (heat loss by low-temperature sink)

    ΔS˙source​=24+273300​=1.0101 kW/K

    ΔS˙sink​=7+273−282.83​=−1.0101 kW/K

    S˙gen​=ΔS˙source​+ΔS˙sink​=0

    Since S˙gen​=0, it complies with the increase in entropy principle.

    #Tutorial 3 (Entropy Change)

    #Question 1

    cFe​=0.45 kJ/kg⋅K

    cw​=4.18 kJ/kg⋅K

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    Q−W=ΔU

    Q−W=mcΔT

    0=mFe​cFe​(Tf​−TFe​)+mw​cw​(Tf​−Tw​)

    Since the tank is insulated, there is no heat gain/loss from the tank.

    Tf​(mFe​cFe​+mw​cw​)=mFe​cFe​TFe​+mw​cw​Tw​

    Tf​=12(0.45)+100(4.18)12(0.45)(350)+100(4.18)(22)​

    Tf​=26.183°C=299.18 K

    ΔsFe​=cFe​ lnT1​T2​​

    ΔsFe​=0.45 ln350+273299.18​

    ΔsFe​=−0.33008 kJ/kg

    Δsw​=cw​ lnT1​T2​​

    Δsw​=4.18 ln22+273299.18​

    Δsw​=0.058813 kJ/kg

    ΔS=mFe​ΔsFe​+mw​Δsw​

    ΔS=12(−0.33008)+100(0.058813)

    ΔS=1.9203 kJ

    #Question 3

    P1​v1​=Rs​T

    v1​=1200.287(17+273)​

    v1​=0.69358 m3/kg

    V=300 l=0.3 m3

    m=v1​V​=0.695380.3​

    m=0.43254 kg

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    Q−W=ΔU

    Qin​−P1​(V2​−V1​)=m(u2​−u1​)

    Qin​−m⋅P1​(v2​−v1​)=m(u2​−u1​)

    Qin​=m[(u2​−u1​)+P1​(v2​−v1​)]

    Qin​=m(h2​−h1​)

    Qin​=mcp​(T2​−T1​)

    15(60)(0.2)=0.43254(1.02)(T2​−290)

    T2​=0.43254(1.02)15(60)(0.2)​+290=698.02 K

    T ds=dh−v dP

    T ds=cp​ dT−PRs​T​ dP

    ds=Tcp​​ dT−PRs​​ dP

    Δs=cp​ lnT1​T2​​−Rs​ lnP1​P2​​

    ΔS=m(cp​ lnT1​T2​​−Rs​ lnP1​P2​​)

    ΔS=0.43254(1.02 ln290698.02​)

    ΔS=0.38753 kJ/K

    #Question 4

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    Q−W=ΔU

    0=U2​−U1​

    U2​=U1​

    mcv​T2​=mcv​T1​

    T2​=T1​

    When a gas expands into a vacuum, it is an unresisted expansion.
    Thus, there is no force and no work is done     W=0.
    Since the tank is insulated,     Q=0.

    T ds=du+P dv

    T ds=cv​ dT+vRs​T​ dv

    ds=Tcv​​ dT+vRs​​ dv

    Δs=cv​ lnT1​T2​​+Rs​ lnv1​v2​​

    ΔS=m(cv​ lnT1​T2​​+Rs​ lnv1​v2​​)

    ΔS=1.5(0.287 lnv1​2v1​​)

    ΔS=1.5(0.287 ln2)

    ΔS=0.29840 kJ/K

    #Tutorial 4 (Reversible Steady-Flow Processes)

    #Question 1

    Compressed as a Saturated Vapor

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    q−w=Δh

    wcomp​=−(h2​−h1​)

    From Table A12, at P1​=140 kPa,

    h1​=hg​=239.19 kJ/kg

    s1​=sg​=0.94467 kJ/kg

    Since the refrigerant is compressed reversibly, s2​=s1​.

    From Table A13, at P2​=0.8 MPa,

    At s=0.9185 kJ/kg, h=267.32 kJ/kg

    At s=0.9481 kJ/kg, h=276.46 kJ/kg

    276.46−267.32h2​−267.32​=0.9481−0.91850.94467−0.9185​

    h2​=275.40 kJ/kg

    wcomp​=−(275.40−239.19)

    wcomp​=−36.211 kJ/kg

    Compressed as a Saturated Liquid

    From Table A12, at P1​=140 kPa,

    v=vf​=0.0007381 m3/kg

    Liquid refrigerant is incompressible, thus specific volume is a constant.

    wrev​=−∫ v dP

    wrev​=−v(P2​−P1​)

    wrev​=−0.0007381(800−140)

    wrev​=−0.487 kJ/kg

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    From Table A2, at Tavg​=400 K,

    cp​=1.013 kJ/kg⋅K

    cv​=0.726 kJ/kg⋅K

    k=1.395

    Exit Temperature

    An isentropic process obeys the relation Pvk=const, where n=k.

    A reversible adiabatic process is an isentropic process.

    Using the isentropic relations of ideal gas,

    T1​T2s​​=(P1​P2​​)kk−1​

    T2s​=300×(95600​)1.3951.395−1​

    T2s​=505.55 K

    Power Input to Compressor

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    q−w=Δh=cp​ΔT

    ws​=−cp​(T2s​−T1​)

    ws​=−1.013(505.55−300)

    ws​=−208.22 kJ/kg

    The above value is the isentropic work input to the compressor.

    #Part (b)

    Power Input to Compressor

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    q−w=Δh=cp​ΔT

    wa​=−cp​(T2a​−T1​)

    wa​=−1.013(550−300)

    wa​=−253.25 kJ/kg

    The above value is the actual work input to the compressor.

    Isentropic Efficiency

    ηcomp​=wa​ws​​

    ηcomp​=253.25208.22​

    ηcomp​=0.82219=82.219%

    #Part (c)

    A polytropic process obeys the relation Pvn=const, where 1<n<k.

    Power Input to Compressor

    Using the isentropic relations of ideal gas,

    T1​T2a​​=(P1​P2​​)nn−1​

    300473​=(95600​)1−n1​

    ln300473​=(1−n1​)ln95600​

    n=1.3281

    wa​=−n−1nRs​(T2a​−T1​)​

    wa​=−1.3281−11.3281(0.287)(473−300)​

    wa​=−200.98 kJ/kg

    Heat Rejected

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    q−w=Δh=cp​ΔT

    q−(−200.98)=1.013(473−300)

    q=−25.731 kJ/kg

    #Part (d)

    An isothermal process obeys the relation Pv=const, where n=1.

    Power Input to Compressor

    wa​=−Rs​T lnP1​P2​​

    wa​=−0.287(300)ln95600​

    wa​=−158.69 kJ/kg

    Heat Rejected

    Using the first law of thermodynamics,

    q−w=Δh=cp​ΔT

    q=w=−158.69 kJ/kg

    Since it’s an isothermal process, heat rejected is equal to work input.

    #Question 2

    Using the first law and taking the control volume as the heat exchanger,

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙Δh

    0=m˙cp​ΔT

    0=m˙a​cpa​​(T2a​−T1a​)+m˙g​cpg​​(T2g​−T1g​)

    Using the ideal gas law, specific volume of air is,

    Pv=Rs​T

    v=950.287(20+273)​

    v=0.88517 m3/kg

    Mass flow rate of air is,

    m˙a​=vV​

    m˙a​=0.885171.6​

    m˙a​=1.8076 kg/s

    Outlet Temperature of the Air

    Substituting the given values into the equation,

    0=1.8076(1.005)(T2a​−293)+2.2(1.1)(95−180)

    T2a​=406.23 K=133.23°C

    Rate of Heat Transfer to the Air

    Using the first law for the air,

    Q˙​−W˙=m˙Δh

    Q˙​=m˙cp​ΔT

    Q˙​=1.8076(1.005)(133.23−20)

    Q˙​=205.7 kJ/s

    Rate of Entropy Generation

    The entropy balance for an open system is,

    ΔSCV​=∑TQ​+∑mi​si​−∑me​se​+Sgen​

    For a steady flow process, ΔSCV​=0.

    Sgen​=∑me​se​−∑mi​si​−∑TQ​

    S˙gen​=(m˙a​s2a​+m˙g​s2g​)−(m˙a​s1a​+m˙g​s1g​)

    S˙gen​=m˙a​(s2a​−s1a​)+m˙g​(s2g​−s1g​)

    S˙gen​=m˙a​Δsa​+m˙g​Δsg​

    Assuming adiabatic heat exchanger (no heat transfer to surroundings), TQ​=0.

    Assuming exhaust gas behaves as an ideal gas,

    S˙gen​=m˙a​(cpa​​ lnT1a​T2a​​−Rs​ lnP1a​P2a​​)+m˙g​(cpg​​ lnT1g​T2g​​−Rs​ lnP1g​P2g​​)

    S˙gen​=1.8076(1.005 ln20+273406.23​)+2.2(1.1 ln180+27395+273​)

    S˙gen​=0.090683 kW/K

    and leaves the condenser as a saturated liquid.

    Compression process takes place in an isentropic compressor unless stated otherwise. Fluid exiting
    the condenser is throttled through an expansion valve, which is not an isentropic process.

    If fluid is throttled with an isentropic turbine, then the process is an isentropic one, and the process
    3-4 will be a vertical line.

    25−2022−20​=3.1698−2.3392P−2.3392​

    Psat@22C​=2.67144 kPa

    Pv3​=ϕ3​Psat@22°C​

    Pv3​=0.5(2.67144)

    Pv3​=1.33572 kPa

    ω3​=P−Pv3​0.622Pv3​​

    ω3​=101.325−1.335720.622(1.33572)​

    ω3​=0.0083091

    Between Cooling and Heating Section

    Specific humidity remains constant during heating, thus ω2​=ω3​.
    Assume heating process occurs at constant pressure, thus Pv2​=Pv3​.

    ϕ2​=Psat@T2​​Pv2​​

    Psat@T2​​=Pv2​=Pv3​

    Psat@T2​​=1.33572 kPa

    Note that relative humidity at state 2 is 100% whereby
    the water vapor is able to condense into liquid water.

    From Table A4,

    At T=10°C, Psat​=1.2281 kPa

    At T=15°C, Psat​=1.7057 kPa

    15−10T2​−10​=1.7057−1.22811.33572−1.2281​

    T2​=11.127°C

    #Part (b)

    Mass of dry air is constant during the entire process,

    ma1​=ma2​=ma​

    Mass of water vapor decreases during dehumidification,

    mv1​=mv2​+mf​

    mf​=mv1​−mv2​

    where mf​ refers to the mass of condensed water

    Mass of water vapor is constant during heating,

    mv3​=mv2​

    Energy balance for the cooling section,

    Ein​=Eout​

    H1​=H2​+Hf​+Qout​

    Qout​=H1​−H2​−Hf​

    where Hf​ is the enthalpy of the condensed water

    Enthalpy before cooling section

    H1​=ma​ha1​+mv1​hv1​

    H1​=ma​cp​T1​+mv1​hg@T1​​

    H1​=ma​(cp​T1​+ω1​hg@T1​​)

    h1​=cp​T1​+ω1​hg@T1​​

    From Table A4,

    At T=30°C, hg​=2555.6 kJ/kg

    At T=35°C, hg​=2564.6 kJ/kg

    35−3034−30​=2564.6−2555.6h−2555.6​

    hg@34C​=2562.8 kJ/kg

    h1​=1.005(34)+0.023884(2562.8)

    h1​=95.380 kJ/kg dry air

    Enthalpy after cooling section

    H2​=ma​ha2​+mv2​hv2​

    H2​=ma​(cp​T2​+ω2​hg@T2​​)

    h2​=cp​T2​+ω2​hg@T2​​

    From Table A4,

    At T=10°C, hg​=2519.2 kJ/kg

    At T=15°C, hg​=2528.3 kJ/kg

    15−1011.127−10​=2528.3−2519.2h−2519.2​

    hg@11.127C​=2521.25 kJ/kg

    h2​=1.005(11.127)+0.0083091(2521.25)

    h2​=32.132 kJ/kg dry air

    Enthalpy of condensed liquid

    Hf​=mf​hf​

    Hf​=(mv1​−mv2​)hf​

    hf​=(ω1​−ω2​)hf@10C​

    hf​=(ω1​−ω3​)hf@10C​

    From Table A4, at T=10°C,

    hf​=42.022 kJ/kg

    hf​=42.022(0.023884−0.0083091)

    hf​=0.65449 kJ/kg dry air

    Heat removed

    Qout​=H1​−H2​−Hf​

    qout​=h1​−h2​−hf​

    qout​=95.380−32.132−0.65449

    qout​=62.594 kJ/kg dry air

    #Part (c)

    Using energy balance for the heating section,

    Ein​=Eout​

    Qin​+H2​=H3​

    Note that for air-conditioning processes, temperature is in degree Celsius.

    Enthalpy after Heating Section

    H3​=ma​ha3​+mv3​hv3​

    H3​=ma​(cp​T3​+ω3​hg@T3​​)

    h3​=cp​T3​+ω3​hg@T3​​

    From Table A4,

    At T=20°C, hg​=2537.4 kJ/kg

    At T=25°C, hg​=2546.5 kJ/kg

    25−2022−20​=2546.5−2537.4h−2537.4​

    hg@22C​=2541.04 kJ/kg

    h3​=1.005(22)+0.0083091(2541.04)

    h3​=43.224 kJ/kg dry air

    Heat Added

    qin​=h3​−h2​

    qin​=43.224−32.132

    qin​=11.092 kJ/kg dry air
